content.value_statement: Architecture documentation often becomes unclear or too detailed for its audience. This skill creates focused C4 Mermaid diagrams for system context, containers, components, deployments, and flows.
actual_capabilities: Creates C4 Context diagrams for users, systems, and external dependencies.
Creates C4 Container diagrams for applications, services, databases, and queues.
Creates Component diagrams when internal structure adds useful detail.
Creates Deployment diagrams for infrastructure nodes and runtime placement.
Creates Dynamic diagrams for numbered request or event flows.
Applies Mermaid C4 syntax guidance and common C4 modeling rules.
limitations: It depends on accurate system information from the user or repository.
It does not verify Mermaid rendering in every target documentation platform.
It should avoid Component diagrams when they add little architectural value.
It cannot replace formal threat modeling or architecture review.

use_cases.title: Document a Product Architecture
use_cases.description: Create context and container diagrams that explain a product to engineers, leaders, and stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Map a Microservices Platform
use_cases.description: Show services, databases, queues, external systems, and ownership boundaries for a distributed platform.

use_cases.title: Explain Production Deployment
use_cases.description: Describe cloud, Kubernetes, or regional deployment structure with clear C4 Deployment diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Context Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a high-level architecture view.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C4 Context diagram for this system: [system name]. Include users, external systems, and main relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Document Containers
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for technical system structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C4 Container diagram for [application]. Show deployable units, databases, queues, technologies, and relationship labels.

prompt_templates.title: Add Component Detail
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for one important service or feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C4 Component diagram for [container or feature]. Include only components that clarify responsibilities and data flow.

prompt_templates.title: Model Deployment and Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request combining runtime and sequence views.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create C4 Deployment and Dynamic diagrams for [workflow]. Show infrastructure nodes, runtime containers, and numbered request steps.

output_examples.input: Create architecture documentation for an e-commerce platform with web, API, order, inventory, payment, and database services.
output_examples.output: Produces a context view for shoppers and external providers, plus a container view for services, databases, queues, and API relationships.

output_examples.input: Diagram the sign-in flow for a web application using an API, auth service, and user database.
output_examples.output: Produces a Dynamic diagram with numbered steps from browser submission through credential validation and database lookup.

output_examples.input: Document production deployment for a cloud service running behind a load balancer with application and database tiers.
output_examples.output: Produces a Deployment diagram showing browser, cloud boundary, load balancer, runtime containers, and data tier relationships.

best_practices: Start with Context and Container diagrams before adding lower-level detail.
Use clear names, technology labels, and action-based relationship labels.
Keep each diagram focused and split large systems into separate views.
anti_patterns: Do not model classes or libraries as deployable containers.
Do not show internals of external systems that your team does not own.
Do not create arbitrary C4 levels outside the standard model.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates C4 architecture documentation using Mermaid diagram syntax and short explanatory context.

faq.question: Which C4 levels are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Context, Container, Component, Dynamic, and Deployment diagrams.

faq.question: Can it document microservices?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for service boundaries, team ownership, queues, topics, and event-driven flows.

faq.question: Does it run external commands?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The skill files only contain markdown guidance and Mermaid examples.

faq.question: Where should generated docs go?
faq.answer: The skill recommends files under docs/architecture with names for context, containers, components, deployment, and dynamic flows.

faq.question: Does it replace architecture review?
faq.answer: No. It helps create clear diagrams, but human review is still needed for correctness and risk decisions.
